As of 315 PM Monday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1...  A cold front brings scattered showers and gusty 
winds tonight, ushering in colder air with sub-freezing temperatures 
in the northwest Piedmont by Tuesday night. 

A cold front moving southeast across central North Carolina will 
trigger scattered light showers across the region through late 
evening, impacting the Triad first late this afternoon and early 
evening before shifting east toward the Triangle and Coastal Plain 
late tonight.
Behind the frontal passage overnight into early Tuesday morning, 
winds will shift to the north northeast and become gusty at times, 
reaching 15 to 20 mph. While skies will clear out quickly across the 
Triad by Tuesday morning, lingering low level moisture behind the 
front will keep partly to mostly cloudy skies in place across the 
Triangle and Coastal Plain through much of the morning before 
scattering out. Some patchy low status and fog are possible in the 
overnight/early morning hours. 

Temperatures will turn noticeably colder behind the front. Overnight 
lows tonight will drop into the low to mid 40s, and despite plenty 
of sunshine by Tuesday afternoon, highs will only reach the mid to 
upper 50s. A reinforcing shot of cold air will then move into the 
area Tuesday night, sending temperatures down below freezing across 
the northwest Piedmont, while areas along and east of US-1 drop into 
the mid to upper 30s.

KEY MESSAGE 2... A dynamic synoptic pattern will support strong 
coastal cyclogenesis that will offer cntl NC widespread rain, some 
possibly heavy, and gusty winds late Wed through early Thanksgiving 
Day. However, uncertainty remains regarding sensible weather details 
owing to both differences in timing and amplitude of mid/upr-level 
features and (possible phasing thereof) across NWP guidance and also 
mesoscale influences from a pattern favorable for upstream 
convection and gravity waves. 

The models unanimously indicate a vigorous shortwave trough now over 
the Four Corners will assume negative tilt while pivoting across the 
Southeast Wed-Wed night and up the South and Middle Atlantic coasts 
on Thanksgiving. However, there remains significant model spread 
regarding what degree, if any, that feature may phase with a trough 
axis accompanying a cyclone forecast to dig sewd from srn AB today 
to the lwr OH Valley by Thanksgiving. 

At the surface, an already strong, ~1035 mb cP high now over the nrn 
Plains is forecast to strengthen in excess of 1040 mb while 
progressing across the Great Lakes and Northeast through 
Thanksgiving morning, before quickly weakening and retreating/ 
progressing offshore through Thanksgiving Day. Meanwhile, a couple 
of areas of low pressure are forecast to develop over the nrn Gulf 
and near wrn Cuba, respectively, by early Wed, with the latter 
forecast to be the dominant of the two while strengthening, possibly 
rapidly, northeastward and along the South Atlantic coast through 
Thanksgiving morning. The coastal low may then track just inland of 
the Middle Atlantic coast through Friday morning, while an inland 
low deepens across the OH Valley and lwr Great Lakes. This pattern 
of cyclogenesis will be of, or most similar to, a Miller B, with 
intervening classical, diabatically enhanced cold air damming over 
cntl NC.  

As previous shifts have noted, temperatures within the CAD regime 
Wed through at least early Thanksgiving Day will be cooler than NBM 
and probably require additional downward revisions in the coming 
days. While nely surface winds will have the potential to gust into 
the 30s mph, CAD stability may protect the near surface layer from 
stronger momentum above, and the strongest MSL pressure gradient 
will probably occur Wed night (when nocturnal stability will be 
maximized). Rainfall amounts have the potential to total 1-3", 
locally higher. However, there are indications that the 
strongest/deepest lift may be relatively short-lived and centered 
upon Wed night, with abrupt drying aloft accompanying a mid-level 
dry slot by Thanksgiving afternoon and in a pattern also favorable 
for gravity waves and upstream convection that may reduce downstream 
QPF. Nonetheless, this will be a dynamic system, with a favorable 
synoptic environment for a widespread, soaking rain throughout cntl 
NC.
